---
# storefront-funnel-lab: microservice storefront with checkout-funnel analytics, on OpenShift (AWS)
cloud_provider: ec2
env_type: ocp4-cluster

__meta__:
  catalog:
    display_name: Storefront Funnel Lab
    category: Labs
  deployer:
    scm_url: https://github.com/agnosticd/agnosticd-v2.git
    scm_ref: main

aws_region: us-west-2
control_plane_instance_count: 3
control_plane_instance_type: m6i.xlarge
worker_instance_count: 3
worker_instance_type: m6i.2xlarge
infra_node_count: 0
ocp4_installer_version: "4.18"

workloads:
  - ocp4_workload_guardrail
  - ocp4_workload_storefront

# Admission policy for the lab namespaces (added for the 2026-10 security baseline)
ocp4_workload_guardrail_replicas: 1
ocp4_workload_guardrail_failure_policy: Fail
ocp4_workload_guardrail_node_selector:
  node-role.kubernetes.io/infra: ""

ocp4_workload_storefront_services: 4
ocp4_workload_storefront_funnel_events: true

answer:
The API server did not fall over, and bigger control-plane nodes would not help.

**What rejected the deployment.** The 500 came from the guardrail admission webhook, not from the API server itself. Job 8840217 failed in `ocp4_workload_storefront : Deploy the storefront services` with "failed calling webhook "vworkload.guardrail.example.io" ... no endpoints available for service "guardrail-webhook"". The API server was up and answering: in the same play it created the storefront-h7ctx namespace and two config maps, and it registered the webhook. It then had to call the webhook for the Deployment, and the webhook had no pod behind it.

**Why the webhook was not running.** Splunk for namespace `guardrail-system` on cluster-h7ctx shows the only controller pod, guardrail-controller-5c8d7f9b6-r2kqp, stuck Pending: `FailedScheduling: 0/6 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector, 3 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/master: }`, and the Deployment at 0/1 replicas available.

**Which settings cause it** (`rhpds/agnosticv` `retail_bu/storefront-funnel-lab/common.yaml`):
- `ocp4_workload_guardrail_node_selector: node-role.kubernetes.io/infra: ""` pins the controller to infra nodes,
- but `infra_node_count: 0`, so the cluster has no infra nodes (3 tainted control-plane nodes plus 3 unlabelled workers), and the pod can never be scheduled;
- `ocp4_workload_guardrail_failure_policy: Fail` makes the webhook fail closed, so with no endpoints every Deployment create in the lab is refused.

**Fix.** Drop the infra node selector (or add infra nodes), and consider `Ignore` for the failure policy during provisioning. Resizing the control plane changes none of this.
